question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>BeO</mi></math> reacts with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>HF</mi></math> in presence of ammonia to give <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mfenced></math> which on thermal decomposition produces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mfenced></math> and ammonium fluoride. Oxidation state of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Be</mi></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mfenced></math> is

solution.text:
BeO  on reaction with HF in the presence of ammonia,  NH42BeF4 is formed which on heating forms BeF2  along with ammonium fluoride. 

BeO+2NH3+4HF→NH42BeF4+H2O

Compound A, is NH42BeF4

NH42BeF4→heatBeF2+2NH4F

Compound B is BeF2

In NH42BeF4 the oxidation state of Be is +2.
